video_title: Alt Season, Zcash, Collectibles & The Tokenization Trade
gist: 0xResearch panel with Blockworks Research's Carlos and Ryan on a crypto rally: SEC buyback FAQ de-risking revenue tokens, declining Bitcoin dominance, Zcash and the multi-store-of-value debate, on-chain collectibles gacha, and tokenized equities second-order plays like lending and neo-banks.

insights.claim: An SEC FAQ released the prior week said token buybacks do not constitute essential managerial efforts when the crypto system is functional, which the host reads as removing unregistered-securities tail risk from revenue-generating tokens such as Hyperliquid and Pump.
insights.speaker: Host (Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Removes a left-tail risk that previously made holders of top-revenue tokens uneasy; expect more upside regulatory surprises from SEC and CFTC rulemaking.
insights.quote: there's not there's not regulatory or or um unregistered securities uh tail risk to those instruments

insights.claim: Ryan argues the SEC buyback FAQ barely moves the market because buybacks by Uniswap were already treated as safe, but it works as a final signal: a team still citing legal reasons for not supporting its token is probably lying or monetizing elsewhere.
insights.speaker: Ryan
insights.so_what: Use refusal to buy back tokens despite clarity as a red flag on team alignment with token holders.

insights.claim: Ryan notes that crypto clarity legislation did not pass and that pseudo-clarity is arriving through SEC and CFTC enforcement letters, which is not permanent and could reverse if Trump loses in 2028.
insights.speaker: Ryan
insights.so_what: Regulatory tailwind is administrative rather than statutory, so it carries a political-cycle expiry risk.

insights.claim: Carlos argues buybacks can be defended even for early-stage crypto protocols as marketing spend, since price strength draws attention and users, unlike equity buybacks at early-stage companies; Derive reportedly raised its buyback allocation from 35 to 50%.
insights.speaker: Carlos
insights.so_what: In crypto, buybacks may be an efficient attention-and-reflexivity tool rather than wasted capital.

insights.claim: Bitcoin dominance rose from a low of 40% to 65% during the 2023-2025 period, and over the past four to five weeks it has declined with broad alt outperformance.
insights.speaker: Host (Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Marks a possible regime change from Bitcoin-dominance to alt outperformance.

insights.claim: Carlos says alt season is effectively already underway but is selective: tokens like Pump, Hop, BBB, Near and Lit are up multiples while Bitcoin is down about 5% year to date, and he expects declining dominance over one to two years, not in a straight line.
insights.speaker: Carlos
insights.so_what: Favor alts with clear fundamentals and revenue; indiscriminate alt bids would make him bearish.

insights.claim: Dispersion where the top-performing coins in the top 100 are all the same flavor regardless of fundamentals is read by Carlos as a late-stage signal for the mini run-up, though not necessarily the bull market.
insights.speaker: Carlos
insights.so_what: Watch breadth quality of the top gainers as a short-term froth gauge.

insights.claim: Since the summer low, about 98% of the host's curated watch list outperforms Bitcoin, versus a prior regime where nearly all names underperformed and drew down more than Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Host (Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: A sharp pivot in relative strength supports rotation further out the risk curve.

insights.claim: The host gives two reasons Bitcoin dominance could fall over one to three years: application tokens becoming investable as revenue accrues to the token, and more instruments functioning as stores of value.
insights.speaker: Host (Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Dominance decline would be fundamentals-driven, not just beta rotation.

insights.claim: Ryan counters that most capital allocators will not venture beyond Bitcoin, so new allocator interest could push Bitcoin dominance back up, and he is not convinced either way.
insights.speaker: Ryan
insights.so_what: Institutional inflows are a risk to the declining-dominance thesis.

themes.theme: Multiple stores of value and Zcash

insights.claim: Ryan argues the set of store-of-value assets will expand beyond Bitcoin because value derives purely from social consensus, and social media plus on-chain trading make forming niche consensus far easier than in the era of physical gold; he treats this as a far-out 30-50 year view.
insights.speaker: Ryan
insights.so_what: Fragmentation of monetary premium into communities (gold, Bitcoin, PSA 10 Charizards, Rolex) is an exploratory long-dated idea.
insights.quote: store value assets, their value is just purely derived from social consensus

insights.claim: Ryan says Bitcoin has flaws, including lack of privacy, possible quantum risk and ossifying too early, and the market is hedging those with Zcash, which he calls the likely ring leader of alternative stores of value.
insights.speaker: Ryan
insights.so_what: Zcash demand is partly a hedge on Bitcoin's technical weaknesses.

insights.claim: Ryan notes that because gold, silver and Bitcoin form such a large store-of-value market, only a small capital shift to alternatives could significantly change relative valuations, for example gold falling to 10 trillion with alternatives absorbing the difference.
insights.speaker: Ryan
insights.so_what: Small reallocations from a huge base can move small alternative assets enormously.

insights.claim: Carlos expects only a handful of store-of-value assets, with Zcash occupying a silver-to-Bitcoin's-gold role like Litecoin once did, and does not expect 10 to 15 such assets.
insights.speaker: Carlos
insights.so_what: Position for Zcash plus one or two others rather than a broad store-of-value basket.

insights.claim: Zcash ETFs are approaching about 1 billion dollars of AUM, and ETFs plus digital asset treasuries together hold roughly 5.6-6% of Zcash supply, which the host cites as evidence that TradFi access is ending Bitcoin's monopoly on store-of-value flows.
insights.speaker: Host (Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Instrument access, not just narrative, is driving Zcash demand.

insights.claim: When asked for a non-Zcash ticker to benefit from the store-of-value meme, a panelist reluctantly picks ETH for its longevity and baked-in monetary premium, while another says XRP could benefit from retail FOMO if Zcash reached 100 billion dollars.
insights.speaker: Panelists
insights.so_what: ETH is the consensus, if reluctant, second store-of-value expression; XRP is a speculative retail spillover.

insights.claim: The fundamental thesis for on-chain collectibles is that existing off-chain markets such as eBay are poor, with high fees and shipping costs, and putting them on chain creates better markets; gacha pack businesses have driven prices by buying large amounts of slabs.
insights.speaker: Ryan
insights.so_what: Gacha demand is the primary price driver for tokenized Pokemon and sports cards.

insights.claim: Secondary-market volume on on-chain collectibles platforms, as opposed to gacha pack-rip volume, is rising sharply, which Ryan calls the most important chart as proof these venues are better than eBay for trading.
insights.speaker: Ryan
insights.so_what: Secondary liquidity validates product-market fit beyond primary gacha sales.

insights.claim: Ryan describes a tokenization barbell: traditional instruments like stocks and ETFs on one end and collectibles on the other, and he finds the collectibles end more compelling because on-chain is clearly the better venue, whereas he would not trade tokenized Tesla over a brokerage account.
insights.speaker: Ryan
insights.so_what: RWAs win where the on-chain form factor is uniquely better, not where it merely replicates brokerage access.
insights.quote: I'm not exactly sure most people would want to trade tokenized Tesla over Tesla through their brokerage account

insights.claim: Coinbase teased an announcement letting users open card packs in its app, likely via a partner protocol rather than sourcing inventory itself; Collector Crypt, Courtyard and Beezie are named as candidates, with Cards (a token) reportedly pumping on it.
insights.speaker: Ryan
insights.so_what: The partner chosen would be a large bullish catalyst for that protocol; a Coinbase tie-up also carries a tops-signal counterpoint since its NFT marketplace launched at the top of NFTs.

insights.claim: Ryan expects every collectible to eventually trade on chain, with gacha expanding to watches, Hot Wheels and rare coins, but predicts a boom-bust cycle because supply of gacha products will outpace demand since crypto users are especially drawn to Pokemon cards.
insights.speaker: Ryan
insights.so_what: Expect overbuilt gacha categories with little adoption; Pokemon-like demand may not transfer.

themes.theme: Tokenized equities, lending and second-order plays

insights.claim: Carlos argues investors overweight DEXs as the way to play tokenized equities: current volume is mostly meme-equity pairings on Uniswap, Raydium and Meteora, and prop AMMs will likely take more share as volume shifts to USD pairs, while money markets that accept tokenized equities as collateral are overlooked.
insights.speaker: Carlos
insights.so_what: Second-order beneficiaries (lending) may offer better exposure than first-order venues.

insights.claim: Morpho and Maple outstanding loans are both at all-time highs despite Bitcoin and ETH being near their lows, and an increasing share of Morpho loans is collateralized by RWAs rather than Bitcoin and ETH; about two-thirds of Onyc is collateral on Kamino, its largest RWA market.
insights.speaker: Host (Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Lending demand is decoupling from crypto-native collateral as RWA issuance grows.

insights.claim: An Aave V4 market on Base for tokenized equities crossed 30 million dollars of tokenized equity supply in the past week, with about 2 million of it deposited, per Carlos.
insights.speaker: Carlos
insights.so_what: Early traction in permissionless equity-collateral lending.

insights.claim: Issuers listing Nvidia, SPY, QQQ or Tesla on chain will not move the needle (about 0.1% of volume) because those are easily accessible; Carlos says issuers should list assets unavailable or illiquid in brokerage accounts, such as discounted crypto-adjacent equities trading near 0.3x mNAV like USD.
insights.speaker: Carlos
insights.so_what: On-chain venues become the most relevant market for niche, distressed names crypto natives understand.

insights.claim: Ryan says first-order effects of bringing equities on chain are unexciting because they can already be traded well elsewhere; the value is in permissionless composability such as lending and consumer apps like Touch Grass and Grail.
insights.speaker: Ryan
insights.so_what: Look for products only possible with permissionless rails.

insights.claim: Carlos argues Athena Pay has structurally better economics than Revolut, Robinhood or EtherFi because, as a stablecoin issuer, it monetizes float from day one through USD mint fees and yield and does not depend on interchange or share net interest margin with partner banks.
insights.speaker: Carlos
insights.so_what: Stablecoin issuers can subsidize better consumer products than bank-partnered neo-banks.

insights.claim: Athena Pay is still early with under 4 million dollars of balances and not open to the public, while an app described as the 'A app' passed 17 million dollars of deposits within a month of iOS early access, offering about 6% on stables with deposit protection.
insights.speaker: Carlos
insights.so_what: The less-discussed savings app has about four times the balances of Athena Pay; Carlos would not fade it despite the Kelp incident.

insights.claim: The shift in crypto is from infrastructure to consumer: stablecoins, tokenization and performant chains are in place, and the question is packaging them into a UX on par with web2 neo-banks, such as EtherFi letting users borrow against stocks permissionlessly.
insights.speaker: Carlos
insights.so_what: Winners will be consumer products using DeFi rails for capabilities traditional neo-banks cannot offer.

insights.claim: The host says Bitcoin holding the 82k level is the key line for confirming a bull market, and that Nasdaq nearing a new all-time high ends a multi-month equity consolidation, providing a constructive backdrop for crypto.
insights.speaker: Host (Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: 82k Bitcoin is the watched support level.

insights.claim: A panelist expects the Robinhood summit to be a nothing burger for Robinhood Chain per consensus, which they view as a good setup for an upside surprise.
insights.speaker: Panelist
insights.so_what: Low expectations skew event risk upward.

insights.claim: October historically tends to be either very early or very late cycle; last year's October included the 10/10 crash, while 2023 and 2024 Octobers preceded November and December rallies.
insights.speaker: Panelist
insights.so_what: Seasonality is ambiguous without cycle position.
